market: NQ (traded as MNQ); ES used as information only via bar['es']
hypothesis: When exactly one of NQ and ES takes out an established RTH session high (low) on a 5m bar and the other does not, NQ moves against that extreme (down after a high, up after a low) over the next hour more than random-direction trades at the same times with the same brackets.
mechanism: The two indices share ~0.9 of their intraday variance through common index/ETF flow. A new session extreme that the other index does not confirm is, by construction, driven by flow specific to one basket (e.g. mega-cap tech in NQ, or non-tech in ES), not by broad demand; resting liquidity above an established high (stops plus breakout orders) is consumed without broad follow-through, so the extreme is more likely to fail. This is the intraday form of the Dow-theory 'confirmation' principle and of the retail 'SMT divergence' setup.

sources.summary: Brown, Goetzmann & Kumar (1998, JF 53(4) 1311-1333), 'The Dow Theory: William Peter Hamilton's Track Record Reconsidered': Hamilton's Dow-theory calls (which require the Industrials and Rails to confirm each other) had positive alpha 1902-1929; neural-net replication beat buy-and-hold out of sample per a secondary summary. Daily/weekly horizon, not intraday; abstract-level check only.
Retail 'SMT divergence' definition for ES/NQ: one market makes a higher high while the correlated one makes a lower high = bearish (mirror for lows). Practitioner indicator, no tested evidence.
Retail SMT divergence script on NQ vs ES pivots. Practitioner, untested.

prior: Weak. No peer-reviewed intraday evidence; the academic source is a different horizon. Closed families nearby (shock fade, VWAP/level fades, CHoCH) all failed and did worse than random direction on ES.
closed_ideas_check: Not on CLOSED_IDEAS.md. Nearest closed: (a) shock_fade fades a large 5m move regardless of level or the other market; here the trigger is a level event (new session extreme vs an established high) conditioned on cross-market non-confirmation, and the move size is irrelevant. (b) CHoCH/swing-structure trades a break of structure in its direction; this fades an extreme and needs the companion. (c) prior-day/OR level touches use fixed external levels; here the level is the developing session extreme. The ES results still make the prior unfavourable, and the report must say so. Family not in data_spend_ledger for NQ or ES.

rules.bars: 5m RTH bars; decision at bar close, fills from the next bar.
rules.session_extremes: For each market m in {NQ, ES}: HI_m(k) = max high of slots 0..k-1 of today, with t_HI_m(k) the slot where it was set (first occurrence); LO_m, t_LO_m likewise. ES values come from bar['es']; a slot with bar['es'] None is skipped for ES extremes and no signal is taken on it.
rules.established: an extreme is established at bar k if it was set at least 6 slots (30 min) before k: k - t_HI_m(k) >= 6.
rules.bearish_signal: at bar k: exactly one market m makes a new high, h_m(k) >= HI_m(k) + 1 tick (0.25 NQ / 0.25 ES), with HI_m(k) established; and the other market m' has h_m'(k) < HI_m'(k). Side = short NQ.
rules.bullish_signal: mirror with lows: exactly one market has l_m(k) <= LO_m(k) - 1 tick with LO_m(k) established, the other has l_m'(k) > LO_m'(k). Side = long NQ.
rules.both: if a bar produces both a bearish and a bullish signal, skip it.
rules.window: signal bars with ET start 10:30 <= mod <= 14:40 (slots 12..62), so the 60-minute time stop ends by 15:45, before the 15:55 flat. In general: slots first_slot..min(last_slot, flat_slot - 15) (half days: 12..26).
rules.news_filter: no signal if a scheduled RTH high-impact release time m satisfies bar_end <= m <= bar_end + 5, as in the ES loop.
rules.once_per_side: at most one bearish and one bullish trade per session. A signal qualifies only if the strategy is flat with no pending order, no exit is being sent on that bar, and the news filter passes; the first qualifying signal of each side is traded, later ones that day are ignored.
rules.entry: market at the next bar's open.
rules.risk: ADR20 = mean of NQ's (RTH high - RTH low) over the prior 20 completed sessions (warmup provides them). Short: stop = c_k + max(HI_NQ_today_incl_k - c_k + 1 tick, M * ADR20), where HI_NQ_today_incl_k is NQ's session high including bar k; long mirrored with the session low. So the stop is always beyond the session extreme and never closer than M * ADR20.
rules.target: 1:1 about the decision close: target = c_k + side * |stop - c_k| (side = +1 long, -1 short).
rules.time_stop: exit at market after 12 completed 5m bars held (60 minutes) without stop or target.
rules.roll_days: no special handling needed: ADR20 uses ranges (contract-invariant) and extremes are intraday.

walk_forward: fixed: no selection; all three M judged by the frozen dev gate, each needing its grid neighbours positive.
expected_trades_per_session: ~0.3-1.0 (divergent extreme events after 10:30 are common on trend-less days); dev ~600-2000 trades per M.
rejection_evidence: Reject if the frozen dev gate fails for every M. Report, not gate: NQ-led vs ES-led divergences (which market made the extreme); longs vs shorts; share of time-stop exits; per-year mean R. A positive result driven only by one of the two cases is a post-hoc split and would need a new pre-registered id.
companion_use: bar['es'] (h, l) per slot; bar['es_roll'] irrelevant (intraday extremes only).
